newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian, German customs halt Burundi arms shipment.
newsitem.headline: Belgian, German customs halt Burundi arms shipment.

text.p: Belgian and German customs have thwarted an attempt to smuggle nine tonnes of military equipment to Burundi, Belgian officials said on Friday.
The equipment consisted of spare parts for Russian-made BRDM-2 armoured patrol vehicles. No guns or ammunition was involved.
Acting on a German tip-off, Belgian officials made the seizure at the beginning of December in a holding area near Brussels National Airport, Belgian customs spokesman Luc De Somere told Reuters.
The parts had been transported to Belgium by road.

"At the time we intercepted the goods there was no indication that they were to be transported to Burundi. However, our German colleagues have told us there was an attempt made there to export the same goods to Burundi," he said.
De Somere said inquiries in both countries were continuing. He declined to say if any arrests had been made in connection with the seizure.

Belgian newspapers reported on Friday the equipment was due to be forwarded to Burundi from Belgium's Ostend airport, fuelling a growing domestic row about the role the airport is playing in arms shipments to Central Africa.

Rebel groups in Burundi, a former Belgian protectorate, have accused Ostend of being a conduit for arms for government forces, which have been subject to an international arms embargo since the military seized power in a coup last July.
A spokesman for Ostend airport declined to comment ahead of an official reaction, slated for Monday, from the Flander's Regional Government.
But a government spokesman told Reuters that customs officers at the airport had recently blocked three other suspect shipments to Africa.
